name: JunkMan's junk's spawn's r4, each game's leftover
why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r4 at the object's +4 as a word, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; JunkMan's spawner of his junk, the third kind's 0x96 (0x080DFF60: push {r4,lr}; push {r0-r3,r5}; movs r0,#0x96; the spawn), sets r0 alone, and its one caller, his update's call before his state runner (0x080C94AE, its bl at 0x080C9562), leaves r4 as his update was entered: in BN4 his +0 byte as BN4's object runner read it (0x13), in BN6 his AI index times four as BN6's Navi frame keeps it across his hook A (0x080F3682: lsls r4,r0,#2; AI 57, 0xE4; his hook A's shim pushes and pops r4, src/emu/xnavi_init.c pre_set). +5 to +7 hold r4's upper bytes, 0 in both. No code 0x96 runs reads its +4 to +7: its block (0x080DFD54-0x080DFF8C: its type routine 0x080DFD54, init 0x080DFD74, update 0x080DFDF2, the hits test and the spawner past them), read for a load or store of +4 to +7 through r5, has none, and its dying is the families' (0x08010560, ThunderMan's 0x70's walk). This byte pair alone, on that object; junkman_v1 at t1 (BN4) and t2 (BN6)
